factors.name: Variant diversity and behavioural entropy
factors.summary: Normalized EPA sequence entropies, variant heterogeneity, n_variants and most eventropy measures load at about 0.85–0.95. The ratio_top_X_variants measures, std_variant_occurrence and mean_variant_occurrence load negatively, so the factor contrasts logs where traces spread over many distinct variants with logs dominated by a few frequent variants. Minimum and typical trace lengths (trace_len_min, trace_len_mode, distinct_activities_min) also load about 0.74, and several of these measures cross-load on Factors 2, 3 and 5.

factors.name: Event volume and trace length
factors.summary: Activity occurrence frequencies, n_events, the non-normalized EPA entropies, central trace-length statistics and average_edit_distance load at 0.7–0.9, and event_density loads -0.69. Since n_traces is constant, this reads as a log-size dimension driven by how many events, and hence how long the traces, a log has. Several trace-length measures cross-load on Factors 1 and 3, and n_events, epa_sequence_entropy and average_edit_distance are flagged as possible Heywood cases.

factors.name: Activity alphabet size and trace-length dispersion
factors.summary: The number of distinct activities and their per-trace maximum and spread load above 0.9. Trace-length dispersion measures (geometric_std, coefficient_variation, iqr, std) load 0.73–0.83, and trace_len_entropy (-0.85) and epa_normalized_variant_entropy (-0.80) load negatively. density_dfg is negative and structure_dfg positive (about ±0.68), consistent with larger alphabets producing sparser directly-follows graphs; the factor combines two notions, and trace_len_max, std and variance cross-load with Factor 2.

factors.name: Concentration on few start and end activities
factors.summary: Location statistics of start activity frequencies (about 0.94–0.98) and of end activity frequencies (0.79–0.88) load positively. The numbers of unique start and end activities and start_activities_std load negatively (about -0.78 to -0.80), so high scores mean traces begin and end with few, frequent activities. n_cut_vertices_dfg and separability_ratio_dfg (about 0.87) join this factor, suggesting more articulation points in the DFG of such logs.

factors.name: Directly-follows graph size and connectivity
factors.summary: Five DFG and succession measures load moderately (0.59–0.66), all with cross-loadings of 0.52–0.55 on Factor 1, and the factor explains only 3.6% of variance. n_edges_dfg, cyclomatic_number_dfg and number_of_successions are linearly dependent according to the warnings, so the factor partly reflects near-duplicate measures.

factors.name: Loops within traces
factors.summary: All five loop measures from the Repetitions group load 0.60–0.88 with small loadings elsewhere, giving a clearly defined though small factor (3.1% of variance). n_traces_with_repetition does not join it and is assigned to Factor 2.

factors.name: Dominant start activity
factors.summary: Only start_activities_max is assigned (0.66), with start_activities_variance (0.59, cross-loading with -0.62 on Factor 4) and start_activities_std (0.49) close behind. It seems to capture the frequency of the most common start activity, separate from the general concentration in Factor 4, but it explains just 2% of variance.

factors.name: Unevenness of end activity frequencies
factors.summary: Two essentially equivalent spread measures of end activity frequencies load about 0.8, with end_activities_max at 0.37. This is a narrow factor carried by two near-duplicate measures, explaining 1.7% of variance.

factors.name: Weak residual of trace-length histogram bins
factors.summary: No measure is assigned. The largest loadings come from histogram bins with low communality (trace_len_hist9 0.55, hist5 0.42, hist8 0.34, hist3 0.31) and from eventropy_lempel_ziv_flattened (0.38). This factor has no clear interpretation.

factors.name: Shape of activity frequency distribution
factors.summary: activities_kurtosis (0.74) and activities_skewness (0.62, also -0.50 on Factor 1) define this factor, which reflects how skewed and heavy-tailed activity occurrence counts are. It rests on two measures and explains 1.5% of variance.

factors.name: Trace-length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: Two single histogram bins load about 0.85 and nothing else is notable. This is a measure-specific factor without a broader meaning.

factors.name: Trace-length histogram bins 1 and 10
factors.summary: Two histogram bins at the extremes of the trace-length distribution load 0.87 and 0.77. It is a narrow, measure-specific factor.

factors.name: Frequency of the rarest activities
factors.summary: Only activities_min is assigned with a moderate loading (0.53), followed by activities_q1 (0.42) and activities_median (0.30). It may reflect how often the least frequent activities occur, but the support is thin.

factors.name: Shape of trace-length histogram
factors.summary: Kurtosis (0.69) and skewness (0.66) of the trace-length histogram load here, but both cross-load on Factor 3 (0.55 and 0.50); trace_len_hist6 adds 0.44. It is a small shape factor of 1.2% of variance.

factors.name: Uninterpretable residual factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned, and the largest loadings are only about |0.23–0.31|, mixing variant occurrence and end activity measures of different sign. It explains under 1% of variance and should not be interpreted.

interpretation.overall:
Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.88 is well above its threshold, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. The 15 varimax-rotated factors explain 89% of variance, but most of this comes from four broad factors (about 69% combined). These are:
- variant diversity/entropy (Factor 1)
- event volume and trace length (Factor 2)
- activity alphabet size and trace-length dispersion (Factor 3)
- concentration on few start/end activities (Factor 4)

Two smaller but coherent factors capture DFG size/connectivity (Factor 5) and loops (Factor 6). Factors 7–15 each explain 2% or less and are carried by one or two measures, often single histogram bins, or by no assigned measure at all (Factors 9 and 15). This suggests the factor count is generous and a solution with fewer factors may be more robust. Trace-length measures cross-load notably among Factors 1–3, and the DFG measures of Factor 5 cross-load on Factor 1.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular because several measures are linearly dependent (e.g. n_edges_dfg, cyclomatic_number_dfg, number_of_successions, activities_q3, trace_len_q3), so results rely on clamped eigenvalues and pseudo-inverses.
n_events, epa_sequence_entropy, epa_sequence_entropy_exponential_forgetting and average_edit_distance reach the communality bound, indicating a possible Heywood case.
n_traces is constant in this dataset, so count measures such as n_variants and activity frequencies effectively act as per-trace ratios, which shapes Factors 1, 2 and 4.
Measure definitions give only the group, so interpretations rest on measure names and group descriptions.
Six trace-length histogram bins are unassigned for low communality, and end_activities_max and cyclicity_dfg are unassigned for low loadings.
Eighteen cross-loadings, mainly among Factors 1, 2, 3 and 5, mean these factors are not cleanly separated.
Many near-duplicate measures (e.g. the EPA entropy variants and the eventropy_knn family) inflate the size and apparent clarity of some factors.

The solution reflects shared variance in this particular set of 2112 logs and depends on the varimax rotation, the 15-factor choice and the measures removed by MSA filtering and cleaning; it does not show causes.
